_comment: The content packs this viewer can offer to download.
A data file rather than a list in the code, so a pack can be added, its
size corrected or its URL moved without touching Python -- and so the set
of things a build offers is inspectable without reading a module.
Every field is required except 'companions' and 'family'.  'copyright' in
particular is mandatory and is checked by a test: the acknowledgements
screen is generated from these entries, so a pack that cannot state its
terms is a pack that would be redistributed unattributed.
'approximate_bytes' is what the user is shown before consenting and what
sets the fetch's size cap; measure it (an HTTP HEAD gives Content-Length)
rather than estimating, since a cap below the real size fails the download
on its last megabyte.
'marker' is a path that proves the pack is already unpacked; empty means
the directory existing and being non-empty is proof enough.
There is deliberately no entry for Alien Arena's base art.  The only
source of it is its own game data, licensed for use solely within its own
engine, so this viewer may neither download it nor read an installed copy.
The symmetry with the Quake 3 entry is inviting and false.
The Unvanquished entries are one package per file, because that is how
that content is published: a map package carries no art and names the
texture packages it draws from in its own DEPS file, which is where each
map's 'companions' list below comes from (SPEC-DPK section 4,
SPEC-UNVDIST section 5).  A map fetched without them renders in grey.
There is deliberately no entry for Unvanquished's player, buildable or
weapon models, nor for its voices, soundtrack or ambient sound.  Those
nine packages state no licence anywhere in the archive (SPEC-UNVDIST
section 1.5): the only terms that reach them are a project-wide statement
in a different package, which is an inference and not a fact, and
SPEC-UNVDIST section E.1 escalates it.  A pack that cannot state its terms
is refused by twig_bb.catalog and left out of the acknowledgements, which
is the outcome that rule exists for.  Two things would have to change
before they could be offered: the licensing question answered by a human,
and a reader for Inter-Quake Model, since the meshes are .iqm and nothing
here loads one yet.

packs.title: Quake 3 replacement textures
packs.copyright: Creative Commons replacement art, ioquake3 community
packs.notes: Independently produced art made to drop in under the base game's own texture names. CC BY-NC-ND 3.0: not licensed for commercial use.

packs.title: OpenArena maps (50 levels)
packs.copyright: OpenArena project, CC BY-SA 3.0 / GPL; Debian main
packs.notes: The levels themselves. Without the two companions they render untextured.

packs.title: OpenArena textures
packs.copyright: OpenArena project, CC BY-SA 3.0 / GPL; Debian main
packs.notes: The art the maps draw with. The largest of the packs by a wide margin.

packs.title: OpenArena base data and shader scripts
packs.copyright: OpenArena project, CC BY-SA 3.0 / GPL; Debian main
packs.notes: Menu art, models, the ambient sounds, and -- the reason a viewer wants it -- the .shader scripts. Many surface names in these maps are shader names rather than file names, and resolve to nothing without them.

packs.title: OpenArena Community Map Pack 1
packs.copyright: Various authors, CC BY-SA 3.0 / GPL; Debian main
packs.notes: Community-made levels, each with its own author. Wants the OpenArena art packs, which is what its maps are built against.
